findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file is missing, unreadable, or not valid UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: external file I/O failure aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error to the caller
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a domain error type. Use `?` to propagate the error: `let text = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))?;

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing into a Vec with no bounds verification
findings.failure_mode: a line with zero commas (empty line, malformed input) causes a panic at runtime via index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use parts.get(0) and handle None with a map_err or early continue with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing into a Vec with no bounds verification
findings.failure_mode: a line with exactly one comma or fewer causes a panic at runtime via index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1) and handle None with a map_err or early continue with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range value strings
findings.failure_mode: malformed numeric input (e.g., "abc" or "99999") aborts the session loader instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use parts[1].parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Value(parts[1].clone(), e))? and propagate through a Result return type

findings.problem: as u16 performs a lossy widening cast from u32 to u16, silently truncating values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value like 70000 silently wraps to 4464, producing incorrect records with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow(parts[1].clone()))? to reject values outside u16 range with a typed error

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec of all comma-separated parts when only the first two are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line, and the pattern masks the fact that malformed lines (wrong field count) are not validated before indexing
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract name and value fields in a single pass, then validate both fields exist before constructing the Record

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is logging/I/O embedded in data-processing logic
findings.failure_mode: side effects inside the data transformation pipeline prevent deterministic behavior, break testability, and couple the core to stdout
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If progress reporting is needed, handle it at the shell boundary outside the pure data transformation

findings.problem: The function returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve or capacity planning before collecting lines
findings.failure_mode: unbounded reallocations as lines are collected; allocation failure during collect returns None with no error handling path
findings.fix: Add a try_reserve on the Vec after reading the file: `let mut records = Vec::with_capacity(text.lines().count()); records.try_reserve(text.lines().count()).map_err(|e| LoadError::Allocation(e))?;

findings.problem: load_sessions performs file I/O (fs::read_to_string) inside a function that is the functional core itself, not a shell boundary
findings.failure_mode: the core is not pure or testable without a real filesystem; the function conflates the action layer (I/O) with the calculation layer (parsing)
findings.fix: Split into two functions: a pure `fn parse_sessions(lines: impl Iterator<Item = &str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>` for the core, and a shell function `fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>` that reads the file and delegates to the pure parser

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure throughput of session loading
no profiler data (perf, flamegraph, or similar) to validate allocation patterns
no allocation tracing (e.g., alloc counters, jemalloc stats) to verify try_reserve intent
no second-ring review artifact (black-hat review or formal contract parity check)
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy) to verify the crate compiles and passes checks
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate contains 8 BLOCKER violations: unwrap on I/O and parse results, unchecked indexing on split output, a lossy width-reducing cast (u32 as u16), I/O side effects in the core, missing try_reserve, parsing without split_once, and the functional core/shell boundary is not separated. All violations must be fixed and verified with cargo test before delivery.
